description_full: Loar Holdings Inc., through its subsidiaries, designs, manufactures, and sells aerospace and defense components for aircraft, and aerospace and defense systems in the United States and internationally. It offers airframe components, structural components, avionics, composites, braking system components, de-ice and ice protection, electro-mechanical, engineered materials, flight controls, fluid and motion controls, environmental, metal forming, molded components, and restraints and safety devices. The company also provides auto throttles, lap-belt airbags, two-and three-point seat belts, water purification systems, fire barriers, polyimide washers and bushings, latches, interior securing devices, hold-open and tie rods, temperature and fluid sensors and switches, carbon and metallic brake discs, fluid and pneumatic-based ice protection, RAM air components, sealing solutions, motion and actuation devices, edge-lighted panels and knobs, and annunciators for incandescent and LED illuminated pushbutton switches, high-performance fans and cooling devices, lighting, Human-Machine Interface products, and bespoke lighting systems, and others. It primarily serves commercial, business jet and general aviation, and defense markets. Loar Holdings Inc. was incorporated in 2017 and is headquartered in White Plains, New York.

financial_summary: Loar Holdings Inc. is a mid-cap industrials business with a $7.1B market cap on $496M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +23% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 6% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 51% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $99M in free cash flow — roughly 20 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.56× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 5.3× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and interest coverage runs at 4.1×.

Net dilution runs at 0.0% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 19% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 1.9× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
